react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-analysis paradigms — RaMP multi-DB ORA, MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA, and Mummichog m/z-direct activity scoring — converge on a single dominant biological signal: perturbation of the androgen and estrogen steroidogenesis axis. RaMP reports KEGG:hsa00140 'Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism' and SMPDB:SMP00068 with identical FDR=5.74e-15 and fold-enrichment=1430, with all five steroid input metabolites (DHT, androstenedione, DHEA, testosterone, estradiol) hitting the pathway. MetaboAnalystR confirms the same KEGG pathway with p=4.36e-07 across 87 pathway members, with the identical five-compound roster. Mummichog independently scores 'Androgen and estrogen biosynthesis and metabolism' (MUMM) as rank-0 with p=8.4e-05, achieving a 100% (11/11) overlap — all five steroid inputs are embedded within the 11-member empirical network, with three additional predicted intermediates (androsterone, 5α-androstane-3,17-dione, androst-5-ene-3β,17β-diol) expanding the implied active sub-network. The Reactome super-pathway 'Metabolism of steroid hormones' (REACT:R-HSA-196071, FDR=2.92e-14) confirms this sits within the broader steroid-hormone metabolism landscape. Butanone (C02845) and sulindac (C01531) are peripheral: butanone is a C4 ketone with no structural role in steroid biosynthesis, and sulindac, a COX-inhibiting NSAID, falls outside the steroidogenesis pathway roster in all three methods. The five core steroids form a contiguous catalytic chain: DHEA → androstenedione → testosterone → DHT (5α-reduced androgen) and androstenedione → estradiol (aromatisation), placing the treatment group's differential abundance at the substrate/product level of both androgen and oestrogen branches. This cross-paradigm consensus — same pathway across ORA (RaMP), KEGG-only ORA (MetaboAnalystR), and m/z-network (Mummichog) — constitutes high-confidence evidence of steroidogenic axis disruption.

react_result.final_narrative_text: RaMP multi-database ORA and Mummichog m/z-direct activity scoring converge on the androgen and estrogen metabolism axis. RaMP-DB identifies SMPDB:SMP00356 (17-Beta Hydroxysteroid Dehydrogenase III Deficiency) as the top hit with FDR=5.74e-15 and fold-enrichment=1430, overlapping all five steroid input compounds. The same five compounds also hit SMPDB:SMP00068 (Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism) and KEGG:map00150 at identical significance. Mummichog independently scores MUMM:androgen_and_estrogen_biosynthesis_and_metabolism as the top pathway with p=8.4e-05, achieving 100% overlap (11 of 11 compounds). The three methods share the same compound roster: DHEA (C01227), androstenedione (C00280), testosterone (C00535), DHT (C03917), and estradiol (C00951). Butanone (C02845) and sulindac (C01531) do not appear in the hit lists for the primary pathway. The five steroid inputs map to the androgen branch (DHEA to androstenedione to testosterone to DHT) and the estrogen branch (androstenedione to estradiol via aromatisation). Driver-metabolite analysis identifies testosterone (C00535) and androstenedione (C00280) as the central nodes connecting both branches within SMPDB:SMP00068.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-analysis paradigms — RaMP multi-DB ORA, MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA, and Mummichog m/z-direct activity scoring — converge on a single dominant biological signal: perturbation of the androgen and estrogen steroidogenesis axis. RaMP reports KEGG:hsa00140 'Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism' and SMPDB:SMP00068 with identical FDR=5.74e-15 and fold-enrichment=1430, with all five steroid input metabolites (DHT, androstenedione, DHEA, testosterone, estradiol) hitting the pathway. MetaboAnalystR confirms the same KEGG pathway with p=4.36e-07 across 87 pathway members, with the identical five-compound roster. Mummichog independently scores 'Androgen and estrogen biosynthesis and metabolism' (MUMM) as rank-0 with p=8.4e-05, achieving a 100% (11/11) overlap — all five steroid inputs are embedded within the 11-member empirical network, with three additional predicted intermediates (androsterone, 5α-androstane-3,17-dione, androst-5-ene-3β,17β-diol) expanding the implied active sub-network. The Reactome super-pathway 'Metabolism of steroid hormones' (REACT:R-HSA-196071, FDR=2.92e-14) confirms this sits within the broader steroid-hormone metabolism landscape. Butanone (C02845) and sulindac (C01531) are peripheral: butanone is a C4 ketone with no structural role in steroid biosynthesis, and sulindac, a COX-inhibiting NSAID, falls outside the steroidogenesis pathway roster in all three methods. The five core steroids form a contiguous catalytic chain: DHEA → androstenedione → testosterone → DHT (5α-reduced androgen) and androstenedione → estradiol (aromatisation), placing the treatment group's differential abundance at the substrate/product level of both androgen and oestrogen branches. This cross-paradigm consensus — same pathway across ORA (RaMP), KEGG-only ORA (MetaboAnalystR), and m/z-network (Mummichog) — constitutes high-confidence evidence of steroidogenic axis disruption.
